A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work despite renaming S-LoRA to SD-LoRA. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.3 are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and weight-space analyses, including additional benchmark results in Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and ablations in Tables 2–6 and the main-text and appendix diagnostic experiments.

M1.justification: v1 Equation (1) and v3 Equation (4) retain the same frozen previous directions, learnable magnitudes, and new task direction. ES-LoRA1/2 correspond to SD-LoRA-RR/KD, retaining rank reduction and least-squares coefficient absorption. Renaming and expanded implementation explanations do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate class-incremental learning on ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, DomainNet, CIFAR100, and CUB200. The additional datasets and diagnostic scenarios in Appendices A.2–A.3 were already present in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: full fine-tuning, L2P, DualPrompt, CODA-Prompt, HiDe-Prompt, and InfLoRA retain their existing participation. Full fine-tuning already appeared in v1; Table 6 continues to omit HiDe-Prompt.

E3.justification: Figure 2(a) changes relative-distance normalization from division by one model's distance to W0 to division by the average of both models' distances, explicitly using Frobenius norms. Benchmark splits, epoch budgets, batch size, and rank settings remain unchanged. Newly disclosed implementation settings do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The weight-proximity diagnostic is revised through symmetric distance normalization and replacement distance matrices in Figures 2(a) and 7. Its scientific question remains the same. The fixed-direction, magnitude-reuse, interpolation, component-ablation, and efficiency analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: v1 describes standard deviations from five runs in Tables 2–4; v3 Section 4.1 reports five-run standard errors instead. Figure 3's legend likewise changes from standard deviation to standard error. The table dispersion values remain identical, leaving the statistical reinterpretation unexplained; no increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 2–6 are retained after matching renamed methods. Relative-distance outputs are replaced under the revised normalization. Additionally, v3 Figure 7(a,b) displays the same heatmap for DomainNet and the DINO condition, whereas v1 showed distinct plots. These are diagnostic-result changes, not demonstrated accuracy improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces the residual-norm-difference assumption with direct operator-norm proximity between task-specific and shared optima. Theorem 1 explicitly targets cumulative rank-k approximations rather than individual principal components. The supporting theorem and proof substantially revise singular-value conditions, block derivations, and error bounds, including explicit transfer of the proximity error.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain a rehearsal-free, end-to-end optimized LoRA method with selection-free inference, a shared-low-loss-region explanation, and two parameter-efficient variants. The revised abstract and contribution list reorganize and foreground these existing claims.

C2.justification: The new conclusion discussion identifies generalization beyond ViT backbones and more theoretically grounded rank-reduction and distillation strategies as unresolved directions. The interpretations concerning early-direction reuse and shared low-loss trajectories remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link, learning rate 0.008, query/value projection placement, shared magnitudes across projections, and magnitude initialization to ones. Conversely, it omits v1's Adam beta values and statement that HiDe-Prompt's stored prototypes were restricted. These are documentation changes, without evidence that the underlying settings changed.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly positions SD-LoRA as a form of model merging and recasts competitors' memory requirements from feature storage to sample rehearsal. It adds Lester et al. (2021) and removes several citations, including Doan et al. (2023) and Lin et al. (2024a,b), while retaining the overall CL/PEFT positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Preliminaries and theory are integrated into the method section, terminology and variant names are standardized, and the conclusion gains discussion and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 are extensively redrawn or restyled, including a redesigned method schematic and replacement of relative-distance line plots with heatmaps. Tables and Algorithm 1 are reformatted and relocated, Table 1's columns are reordered, and the overall layout is reorganized.

improvement.justification: v3 improves exposition and supplies useful implementation details and a code link. However, it relabels unchanged table dispersions as standard errors, duplicates a heatmap across different Figure 7 conditions, and its rewritten Appendix A.1 prints a B update inconsistent with its stated gradient. These unresolved reporting and mathematical issues counterbalance the clarity gains, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
